draft.title: The UN and the Security Council
card: The United Nations (UN) is an organisation of states formed after World War II. Its Charter is its founding treaty.
The Charter bans states from using force against other states. There are two exceptions: self-defence, and force authorised by the Security Council.
The Security Council has 15 members. Five are permanent: China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States.
Each permanent member can veto a decision. A veto by any one of the five blocks a decision, even if other members vote for it.
draft.remember: Force is banned unless it is self-defence or the Security Council authorises it, and any permanent member can veto.

a.q: Under the UN Charter, when may a state lawfully use force against another state?
opts: In self-defence, or when the Security Council authorises it
When its own government decides the other state is a threat
When most UN member states say they support the action
When it has the support of at least one permanent member
a.why: The Charter allows only two exceptions: self-defence and Security Council authorisation. Support from one permanent member is not enough, because the Council must make a decision and no permanent member can veto it.
a.clue: The Charter names two exceptions only.

b.q: A Security Council resolution to authorise force is backed by 14 of the 15 members. One permanent member votes against it. What is the result?
opts: The resolution is blocked by the veto
The resolution passes, as 14 is a large majority
The resolution passes, but only for a limited time
The resolution goes to the other four permanent members
b.why: A veto from any one permanent member blocks a decision, even if all other members vote for it. The size of the majority does not matter, so the tempting answer that 14 votes is enough is wrong.
b.clue: Think about what a permanent member's veto can do.

a.best: In self-defence, or when the Security Council authorises it

b.best: The resolution is blocked by the veto
